flashcards.back: The length of a curve along a circle: the angle-over-360 fraction of the full circumference 2 pi r.
A slice of a circle bounded by two radii and an arc; its area is the angle-over-360 fraction of pi r squared.
One third of base area times vertical height: three identical pyramids fill the prism on the same base with the same height.
A perfectly round solid where every surface point is the radius r from the centre; its volume is 4/3 pi r cubed.
The multiplier on lengths when a shape grows; areas multiply by its square and volumes by its cube.

Doubling a length doubles lengths, so area feels like it doubles too. Area scales with the square of the radius: double the radius and the area quadruples. In class, draw circles of radius 3 cm and 6 cm on squared paper: the small disk covers 9 pi worth of squares and the big one 36 pi, and four small disks tile the big one exactly.
flashcards.front: Doubling the radius doubles the area of a circle.
